units.title: A jet collection became a named, typed thing
units.what: jet_collection_settings carries 9 fields. A fixed-R collection reads R, recombination_scheme, strategy; a variable-R one reads rho, Rmin, Rmax, pt_min instead. The algorithm string decides which branch runs, so the two parameter sets never mix.
units.why: VR jets are not a fixed-R jet with a different number in the R slot. They have no single R at all — the radius is a function of rho and the jet's own pT, clamped between Rmin and Rmax. Reusing the R field would have made a meaningless value mandatory.

units.title: The YAML is validated, not trusted
units.what: 3 explicit checks. Every VR parameter is read with getValue rather than getValueOrDef, so a missing rho is an error rather than a silent default.
units.why: A VR collection with a wrong radius law produces jets that look plausible and are wrong. The failure has to happen at configure time, before any events are read.

units.title: Clustering through the fjcontrib plugin
units.what: A VariableRPlugin in AKTLIKE mode is wrapped in a JetDefinition and handed to the event's cluster sequence. delete_plugin_when_unused() hands the plugin's lifetime to FastJet.
units.why: This is the single line that needs the build changes: VariableRPlugin lives in fjcontrib and is a FastJet plugin, which is why the link surface had to grow by fastjetplugins and both SISCone libraries.

units.code: 236              const double effectiveR = std::min(Rmax, std::max(Rmin, rho / pj.pt()));
units.title: Flavour tagging by the jet's own radius
units.what: b, c and τ association uses effectiveR = min(Rmax, max(Rmin, rho / pT)) — the radius that jet actually had — instead of a fixed cone. W, Z and h association still uses a hard-coded ΔR < 1.0, marked @todo Make selectable? in the source.
units.why: Matching a 20 GeV VR jet and a 500 GeV VR jet with the same cone would mis-tag both, in opposite directions. The whole point of a variable radius is that the catchment shrinks with p<sub>T</sub>, and the tagging has to follow it.

units.title: The event stores cluster sequences by name
units.what: emplace_clusterseq(particles, jetdef, key) keeps one cluster sequence per collection name, and the event owns it. The getter was also fixed: it used to dereference the result of find() without checking for end().
units.why: Multiple named collections coexist in one event, and not every collection exists on every path — the parton and LHEF readers skip VR entirely. Asking for a collection that was never filled is normal, so it had to stop being undefined behaviour.

units.title: VR collections opt out of detector smearing
units.what: std::vector jetcollections_no_smear; is filled from the VR collection keys, and BuckFast skips those collections in two loops: jet-momentum smearing, and the pass that clears b-tags outside |η| > 2.5.
units.why: The BuckFast jet smearing is tuned for calorimeter jets with a fixed radius. VR track jets are a different object with different resolution, so applying the same smearing would be worse than applying none.

units.title: Two readers decline VR outright
units.what: 2 sites continue past any VR collection: the parton-level Pythia conversion and the LHEF reader.
units.why: VR track jets are built from charged-particle tracks. A parton-level or LHE-level event has no tracks to cluster, so producing a collection there would be inventing an object rather than reconstructing one.
